currentContext.business: Deep Industries Limited supplies equipment and services to oil and gas field operations on rental, charter-hire and dry-lease terms rather than selling assets outright. It began with natural gas compression in the 1990s and has added gas dehydration, drilling and workover rigs, integrated project management, charter hire of entire gas processing facilities, offshore support services and, most recently, production enhancement of mature fields. Its customers are major oil and gas producers, public sector undertakings, private sector companies and multinationals, and it states it caters to the upstream, midstream and downstream segments with a presence in drilling, gas gathering, gas processing and gas transmission and distribution.

Natural Gas: Charter hire of entire natural gas processing facility (Project Jaya)
Natural Gas Compression (gas engine driven compressor packages, turnkey)
Natural Gas Dehydration (Build, Own and Operate / charter hire)
Offshore services: Platform Support Vehicles (PSV), Anchor Harding Tugs Supply Vessel (AHTS)
Production Enhancement: Comprehensive services to enhance production of matured fields

currentContext.strengths: Charter-hire / Build-Own-Operate model that converts EPC work into recurring charter-hire revenue - stated as a unique proposition in the industry, exemplified by Project Jaya where the entire gas processing and produced-fluid network from wellhead to transportation point was delivered on charter hire|Stated to be the largest natural gas compression service provider in India on chartered-hire basis, with three decades of compression projects for public and private sector clients|Stated to be the pioneer of Build-Own-Operate gas dehydration systems in India and one of the country's largest gas dehydration service providers|Breadth of portfolio - more than 70% of post-exploration value-chain services under one roof; describes itself as the first Indian company to offer integrated solutions and the only company combining upstream and midstream service provision|Owned fleet: 20 onshore rigs (14 workover rigs of 30T to 150T and 6 drilling rigs of 1000 Hp), and capability to supply drilling, workover, completion and production equipment on charter, rental and dry-lease basis|Fully mobile units allow resources to be transported to any part of the country within a matter of months|Integrated onshore plus offshore reach after acquiring Dolphin Offshore Enterprises (India) Limited through NCLT in 2022|Qualification credentials: approved drilling contractor with Kuwait Oil Company; 16 years of long-term drilling and workover rig contracts with PSUs and private E&P companies|Balance-sheet position described as a judicious balance of liquidity and debt, positioning the company to meet expansion requirements seamlessly
currentContext.strategies: Grow through four service lines - production enhancement contracts, charter hire of entire gas processing facilities, integrated project management services and offshore support services - which management says are all expected to drive growth over the next few years|Convert EPC work into charter-hire services, retaining ownership of gas processing and dehydration assets on a Build-Own-Operate / charter-hire basis rather than selling them|Enter higher-capacity onshore drilling rigs under Integrated Project Management, citing high demand for onshore drilling rigs|Expand the rig business into overseas markets; the Company is an approved drilling contractor with Kuwait Oil Company, and subsidiary Deep International DMCC has acquired gas compression packages in the USA to serve Middle East opportunities|Build out the offshore/marine services business through the subsidiary acquired via NCLT, which is described as actively pursuing sustainable offshore opportunities|Venture into the Green Hydrogen business under an MOU, to bid for and execute green hydrogen tenders and contracts|Maintain a disciplined focus on cost optimisation and operational efficiency, and leverage technology|Maintain a judicious balance between liquidity and debt so that expansion requirements can be met without balance-sheet strain|Recruit highly skilled technical staff and own fuel-efficient, latest equipment, positioned to service oil & gas markets in India and globally|The Board frames dividends against a written Dividend Distribution Policy, and for FY2025-26 recommended a final dividend of Rs 2.50 per Rs 5 equity share, put to members as an ordinary resolution at the 20th AGM and payable out of the profits of the Company. Alongside this the Board has approved introducing an Employee Stock Option Scheme, subject to shareholder approval and an enabling alteration of the Articles, to align employee incentives with long-term growth. Material related-party transactions are put to members for prior approval under Regulation 23(4) on the basis of Audit Committee and Board approval, and the Company also extends or avails corporate guarantees in lieu of loans within that approved framework. Beyond this the bundle contains no stated reinvestment, leverage or buyback philosophy.|Gas-based engines as the environmental positioning: BRSR material issue 1, 'Access and affordable clean energy for all', is flagged as an Opportunity with positive financial implications on the basis that all of the Company's gas processing equipment runs on gas based engines using natural gas as fuel, which the Company describes as a green form of gas enabling less carbon emission. The same claim is repeated in the MD&A 'Green Initiative' section.|MOU signed to venture into the Green Hydrogen business, presented in the MD&A Green Initiative section as the route to adding a new low-carbon line to the service portfolio.|Human capital management is the second BRSR material issue, flagged as an Opportunity, on the basis that strong human capital sustains business growth; the Company states it provides a conducive work environment, systematic appraisal, periodic training and annual campus hiring.|CSR focus stated as education, working with underprivileged and affirmative populations to improve livelihood and overall development of the communities served (BRSR Section B item 7, director's ESG statement).|ESG oversight and training: three training and awareness programmes each for the Board of Directors and KMP, with 100% coverage, covering cybersecurity and data privacy, ESG principles, risk management and internal controls, and anti-corruption and ethical conduct; seven programmes for workers on fire safety, mines vocational training and first-aid.|Vigil Mechanism and Whistle Blower Policy formulated for directors and employees to report unethical practices and suspected mal-practices, supplementing an internal control mechanism reviewed by the Internal Auditor and management.|No quantified ESG targets: BRSR Section B item 5 ('Specific commitments, goals and targets set by the company with defined timelines, if any') and item 6 (performance against them) are printed as '-' for all nine principles, and item 4 names no external code, certification, label or standard adopted, stating only that the Business Responsibility Policy is based on the National Voluntary Guidelines. The Company therefore discloses no dated, measurable ESG target.
currentContext.expansion: Deep Industries expands mainly by adding owned, mobile service assets that are then let on charter hire, rather than by building plants. The MD&A describes an owned fleet of 20 onshore rigs - 14 workover rigs of 30T to 150T and 6 drilling rigs of 1000 Hp - deployable across deserts, eco-sensitive areas and mountain terrain, and gas dehydration units commissioned at capacities of up to 10 LSCMD on a Build-Own-Operate basis. Project Jaya is described as the first project where the entire gas processing and produced-fluid network from wellhead to the transportation point was delivered on a charter-hire basis. The stated forward expansion levers are: entering higher-capacity onshore drilling rigs under Integrated Project Management on the back of high onshore rig demand; expanding the rig business overseas, where the Company is an approved drilling contractor with Kuwait Oil Company and subsidiary Deep International DMCC has acquired gas compression packages in the USA to serve Middle East opportunities; scaling gas compression capacity as outsourcing of that service increases; growing offshore/marine services through the Dolphin Offshore business acquired via NCLT in 2022; and an MOU to enter the Green Hydrogen business. Management states the Company's liquidity and resource base position it to meet expansion requirements seamlessly. No rupee capex programme, project cost or commissioning timetable is stated anywhere in this bundle; the only rupee figure is the capital-commitments named disclosure. BRSR Principle 2 states that the percentage of R&D and capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts is Nil.
currentContext.mdna: Management frames the Indian oil & gas sector as undergoing a structural rebalancing, with the Government accelerating its resolve to reduce import dependence amid global supply-side disruptions|Government targeting a USD 500 billion energy infrastructure opportunity by 2030 with heavy emphasis on domestic exploration and production, under the Aatmanirbhar Bharat vision|Shift by PSUs from captive to outsourced oil and gas support services is explicitly called out as an opportunity for Deep|Rising market demand for gas compression services and an increasing trend of outsourcing that specialised service|Higher demand for skilled labour, oilfield services and equipment as upstream activity expands|Policy pipeline: HELP and the DGH target of expanding India's active exploration area to 1 million sq km by 2030, and convergence of the 10th and 11th OALP bidding rounds|Midstream expansion - growth in the gas pipeline transmission network and rising LNG imports creating opportunity for LNG terminal operation and EPC services|Downstream expansion - 23 refineries with export-oriented infrastructure planned, CGD network development, and a planned expansion of the natural gas pipeline network by about 10,805 km from ~24,945 km operational to nearly 35,750 km|Management's stated positioning: India's only integrated onshore and offshore oil & gas service provider with over 30 years of operational legacy, described as uniquely positioned to capitalise on this investment cycle|"A constantly growing revolving order book ensuring robust revenue visibility" - stated qualitatively, with no order-book value disclosed in this bundle|"A healthy, expanding bidding pipeline driven by heightened domestic E&P activity"|A Rs 1,402 crore production enhancement contract from ONGC for 15 years, under which production operations have commenced, is the one contract quantified in the MD&A

risks.risk: Customer concentration - dependency on a few clients
risks.note: Named by the Company in both the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' paragraph and the BRSR material-issues table: being in a niche services segment related to the oil and gas industry, where only a few companies are present in the country, the Company sees a risk of dependency on few clients. Stated mitigation is expanding the customer base outside the country. Financial implication flagged as negative.

risks.risk: Procurement risk - inability to procure rightly configured equipment in a timely manner
risks.note: Flagged in the MD&A and repeated as a BRSR material issue with negative financial implications. The business model is asset-led charter hire, so failure to source correctly specified rigs, compressors and dehydration packages on time directly constrains contract execution. Stated mitigation is continuous training programmes and staying updated on the latest equipment availability.

risks.risk: Scarcity of skilled personnel in the market
risks.note: Listed first among the Company's concerns in the MD&A 'Risks and Concerns' paragraph. The services are manpower-intensive and technical; the Company responds by appointing experienced professionals in technical and commercial departments and, as a stated strategic policy, hiring a new pool of talent every year from reputed technical/petroleum institutes through campus selection.

risks.risk: Safety exposure as a service provider to a high-risk industry
risks.note: The MD&A states that, being a service provider to a high risk industry, safety of employees is the utmost priority and that the Company ensures compliance with all rules and regulations while providing services. Worker training in the year covered fire safety, mines vocational training and first-aid. The Health, Safety & Environment paragraph is cut off mid-word in this bundle, so the full disclosure could not be read.

risks.risk: Single-industry exposure to Indian oil & gas capex and policy
risks.note: The whole growth narrative rests on Indian upstream activity, PSU outsourcing and government policy support, with no offsetting business line disclosed. The MD&A's own discussion of financial performance reports revenue under a single nature-of-services description, and management describes the segment as one in which only a few companies operate in the country - so both demand and competition are concentrated.

risks.risk: No dedicated Board-level ownership of sustainability, and no independent assessment of policies
risks.note: BRSR Section B item 9 states the Company does not currently have dedicated Board-level leadership for sustainability related issues; the CSR, Risk Management and Stakeholder Relationship Committees look at broader ESG aspects under Board guidance. Item 11 states no independent assessment or evaluation of the working of its policies has been carried out by an external agency for any of the nine principles.

risks.risk: ESG policies do not extend to value-chain partners
risks.note: BRSR Section B item 3 answers 'No' for all nine NGRBC principles on whether the enlisted policies extend to value chain partners. For a contractor deploying equipment and manpower at client wellsites, conduct and HSE exposure in the supply chain is left outside the policy perimeter.

thesis: Asset-light-ish integrated oilfield services play riding India's multi-year domestic E&P investment cycle. Four verticals (onshore drilling rigs, workover/gas processing & compression, production enhancement/PEC, offshore support via Dolphin) all growing. ~INR2,967 cr order book gives multi-year visibility; management guides 30-35% revenue growth for FY27 and a similar pace into FY28. High EBITDA margins (46-48%) and low net debt support self-funded growth (QIP paused). Key swing factors: PEC ramp (INR150 cr/yr potential), Dolphin offshore expansion, and new ONGC/GAIL order inflow.

One-offs/notes: (a) Dolphin barge had higher raw-material/operating expense this quarter from one-time client-required repairs (treated as one-off, not recurring). (b) Rajahmundry/Andhra PEC well gas-leakage/fire incident — one rig partially destroyed (insured, well + rig covered); contained in 5 days, no casualty; ~2-3 month deferral of incremental PEC revenue. (c) Prior FY25 Q4 had ~INR250 cr Kandla write-off; potential further ~INR200 cr doubtful receivables but NO provisioning expected this FY.
guidance (critical):
- **Revenue growth:** >30-35% growth for FY27, and "similar growth" expected for FY28 (order-inflow dependent). Implied FY26 ~INR850 cr (investor estimate, not denied).
- **Margin:** EBITDA margin guided to stay in 46-48% range.
- **Order inflow:** Current bidding pipeline ~INR800 cr (excludes offshore bids); win rate ">50%" in some verticals; expect good Q4 conversion (1-2 already L1). Offshore bids still at evaluation stage (no bids submitted yet).
- **PEC:** ~INR150 cr/yr potential, fully reached on a full-year basis by FY28 (FY27-28); 2-3 month delay from incident. New PEC contracts may also come up.
- **Rig/asset additions:** China-sourced onshore rigs — one already deployed (Dec); second to be deployed ~first week of March (Q4); will add incremental Q4 revenue. New higher-capacity rigs being pursued ("need of India today").
- **Provisioning:** No further Kandla write-off/provisioning expected in FY26.
order book & pipeline (ongc/oil tenders):
- Order book INR2,967 cr (as on date), plateaued around INR3,000 cr for several quarters.
- Q3 order wins ~INR140 cr (below typical INR200-300 cr) — attributed to timing; spillover into Q4; 1-2 tenders at L1.
- Bidding pipeline ~INR800 cr (onshore/services only; excludes offshore).
- Regular tender flow from ONGC and other O&G producers; ONGC announced major FY27 capex — new order series anticipated.
- New GAIL contract won (fresh, not renewal). Supreme Court/High Court ONGC arbitration (~INR180 cr claim) — already won at arbitration & commercial-court levels; resolution expected in next 3-6 months.
segment detail:
- **Gas services (dehydration/compression/gas processing):** core; running multiple process plants; steady demand.
- **Onshore drilling & workover rigs:** healthy utilization; new China rigs being deployed; pursuing higher-capacity rigs.
- **PEC / Production Enhancement (ONGC):** new vertical, 40 wells; ~INR20 cr in Q3; producing above baseline; one well impacted by incident; revenue share = incremental gas over baseline.
- **Offshore support (Dolphin Offshore):** fully contributing during quarter; Prabha Barge (African waters), HF Hunter (JV, Mexico→Argentina, day rates "in line"); support vessels (barge, anchor-handling tugs, diving support) seeing good global demand.
growth / optionality:
- Offshore expansion via Dolphin — global support-vessel demand; possible Venezuela/Americas opportunity (early stage); vessel acquisition only on firm order ("Deep policy").
- Integrated projects / more PEC contracts; backward integration via Kandla hydrocarbon fluids (input to drilling).
- Export/international optionality (Africa, Argentina, possibly Americas).
- Longer-term optionality (not firm): **CCUS** (INR20,000 cr scheme — strong tech overlap on CO2 compression/transport/injection, SLB/Halliburton analog), **compressed biogas** (5% mandate mandatory FY29 — compression/dehydration as a service), **hydrogen**. Management "actively evaluating" but nothing firm.
margins & cost: - EBITDA margin 47.6% (Q3), 46.3% (9M avg); guided 46-48%. Driven by tight cost control. Dolphin one-time repair cost inflated raw-material/opex this quarter (one-off). Growth volume-led, not price-led.
capex (rig/asset additions): - China onshore rigs (one deployed Dec, second early-March Q4). PEC capex ~INR160 cr (earlier plan). Regular gas-processing-plant and rig capex ongoing. Backward-integration vertical (FY27-targeted, H2 FY27) needs some — but "not major" — capex. Vessel acquisition under Dolphin contingent on firm order. India-US trade deal duty cut could reduce capex cost on US-imported compressors.
capital allocation: - **QIP paused** — not proceeding now (management cited undervalued share price). Capex funded via internal accruals + debt; "very low debt," comfortable raising more. Acquisitions (Dolphin vessel / targets) may be deferred to next year; may revisit equity at "opportune time."
risks:
- **Client concentration:** heavy ONGC/GAIL (PSU) reliance; diversification (Oil India, GSPC LNG, Vedanta, Selan) is gradual, "won't be immediate." PSU receivable cycle a watch-item (mgmt comfortable, 30-yr relationship).
- **Oil-price-linked E&P capex:** mgmt argues low sensitivity — revenue is "inevitable" support services, least impacted by crude price.
- **Execution / operational:** Andhra/Rajahmundry PEC well incident (rig partially destroyed, 2-3 month revenue deferral; no contractual penalty, insured). Order-win lumpiness (Q3 weak inflow). Kandla ~INR208 cr doubtful receivables (potential future provisioning).
- **Order-book plateau** at ~INR3,000 cr — dependent on ONGC FY27 capex converting.
management tone: Confident and consistent; emphasized 3 years of steady delivery, safety/execution discipline, capital efficiency. Calm handling of incident and write-off questions. Reiterated discipline (capex only on firm order). Bullish on India energy-independence macro.
non-obvious points:
- PEC revenue = only the **incremental** gas above baseline counts (so headline contract size overstates near-term revenue).
- No contractual penalty for the well incident — "not producing is itself the penalty"; ONGC ex-gratia (INR10,000 to ~5,000 families, 100-bed hospital) is ONGC CSR, no liability on Deep.
- Kandla acquired for only ~INR2 cr (from IBC) — write-offs (~INR250 cr done + ~INR200 cr potential) relate to legacy receivables NOT cash paid by Deep; real motive was hydrocarbon-fluids backward integration + real estate.
- China-sourced rigs (supply chain note); vessels float region-to-region (Mexico→Africa/Argentina) at comparable day rates.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ India domestic E&P / gas-infrastructure capex cycle (USD100bn by 2030) — broad oilfield-services tailwind; ONGC FY27 capex.
- ✅ Import-substitution / India-US trade deal — potential lower capex cost on imported compressors.
- ⭐ CCUS / compressed-biogas / hydrogen optionality — adjacent service markets (compression/dehydration) Deep could enter.

- **PEC:** ~INR150 cr/yr potential, fully reached on a full-year basis by FY28 (FY27-28); 2-3 month delay from incident. New PEC contracts may also come up.
- **Rig/asset additions:** China-sourced onshore rigs — one already deployed (Dec); second to be deployed ~first week of March (Q4); will add incremental Q4 revenue. New higher-capacity rigs being pursued ("need of India today").
- **Provisioning:** No further Kandla write-off/provisioning expected in FY26.
order book & pipeline (ongc/oil tenders):
- Order book INR2,967 cr (as on date), plateaued around INR3,000 cr for several quarters.
- Q3 order wins ~INR140 cr (below typical INR200-300 cr) — attributed to timing; spillover into Q4; 1-2 tenders at L1.
- Bidding pipeline ~INR800 cr (onshore/services only; excludes offshore).
- Regular tender flow from ONGC and other O&G producers; ONGC announced major FY27 capex — new order series anticipated.
- New GAIL contract won (fresh, not renewal). Supreme Court/High Court ONGC arbitration (~INR180 cr claim) — already won at arbitration & commercial-court levels; resolution expected in next 3-6 months.
segment detail:
- **Gas services (dehydration/compression/gas processing):** core; running multiple process plants; steady demand.
- **Onshore drilling & workover rigs:** healthy utilization; new China rigs being deployed; pursuing higher-capacity rigs.
- **PEC / Production Enhancement (ONGC):** new vertical, 40 wells; ~INR20 cr in Q3; producing above baseline; one well impacted by incident; revenue share = incremental gas over baseline.
- **Offshore support (Dolphin Offshore):** fully contributing during quarter; Prabha Barge (African waters), HF Hunter (JV, Mexico→Argentina, day rates "in line"); support vessels (barge, anchor-handling tugs, diving support) seeing good global demand.
growth / optionality:
- Offshore expansion via Dolphin — global support-vessel demand; possible Venezuela/Americas opportunity (early stage); vessel acquisition only on firm order ("Deep policy").
- Integrated projects / more PEC contracts; backward integration via Kandla hydrocarbon fluids (input to drilling).
- Export/international optionality (Africa, Argentina, possibly Americas).
- Longer-term optionality (not firm): **CCUS** (INR20,000 cr scheme — strong tech overlap on CO2 compression/transport/injection, SLB/Halliburton analog), **compressed biogas** (5% mandate mandatory FY29 — compression/dehydration as a service), **hydrogen**. Management "actively evaluating" but nothing firm.
margins & cost: - EBITDA margin 47.6% (Q3), 46.3% (9M avg); guided 46-48%. Driven by tight cost control. Dolphin one-time repair cost inflated raw-material/opex this quarter (one-off). Growth volume-led, not price-led.
capex (rig/asset additions): - China onshore rigs (one deployed Dec, second early-March Q4). PEC capex ~INR160 cr (earlier plan). Regular gas-processing-plant and rig capex ongoing. Backward-integration vertical (FY27-targeted, H2 FY27) needs some — but "not major" — capex. Vessel acquisition under Dolphin contingent on firm order. India-US trade deal duty cut could reduce capex cost on US-imported compressors.
capital allocation: - **QIP paused** — not proceeding now (management cited undervalued share price). Capex funded via internal accruals + debt; "very low debt," comfortable raising more. Acquisitions (Dolphin vessel / targets) may be deferred to next year; may revisit equity at "opportune time."
risks:
- **Client concentration:** heavy ONGC/GAIL (PSU) reliance; diversification (Oil India, GSPC LNG, Vedanta, Selan) is gradual, "won't be immediate." PSU receivable cycle a watch-item (mgmt comfortable, 30-yr relationship).
- **Oil-price-linked E&P capex:** mgmt argues low sensitivity — revenue is "inevitable" support services, least impacted by crude price.
- **Execution / operational:** Andhra/Rajahmundry PEC well incident (rig partially destroyed, 2-3 month revenue deferral; no contractual penalty, insured). Order-win lumpiness (Q3 weak inflow). Kandla ~INR208 cr doubtful receivables (potential future provisioning).
- **Order-book plateau** at ~INR3,000 cr — dependent on ONGC FY27 capex converting.
management tone: Confident and consistent; emphasized 3 years of steady delivery, safety/execution discipline, capital efficiency. Calm handling of incident and write-off questions. Reiterated discipline (capex only on firm order). Bullish on India energy-independence macro.
non-obvious points:
- PEC revenue = only the **incremental** gas above baseline counts (so headline contract size overstates near-term revenue).
- No contractual penalty for the well incident — "not producing is itself the penalty"; ONGC ex-gratia (INR10,000 to ~5,000 families, 100-bed hospital) is ONGC CSR, no liability on Deep.
- Kandla acquired for only ~INR2 cr (from IBC) — write-offs (~INR250 cr done + ~INR200 cr potential) relate to legacy receivables NOT cash paid by Deep; real motive was hydrocarbon-fluids backward integration + real estate.
- China-sourced rigs (supply chain note); vessels float region-to-region (Mexico→Africa/Argentina) at comparable day rates.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- ✅ India domestic E&P / gas-infrastructure capex cycle (USD100bn by 2030) — broad oilfield-services tailwind; ONGC FY27 capex.
- ✅ Import-substitution / India-US trade deal — potential lower capex cost on imported compressors.
- ⭐ CCUS / compressed-biogas / hydrogen optionality — adjacent service markets (compression/dehydration) Deep could enter.

---
qoq log: - **Q3 FY26 (this call, 06-Feb-2026):** Rev INR221.5 cr (+43.1% YoY), 9M INR642 cr (+57%); EBITDA margin 47.6% (Q3) / 46.3% (9M); PAT INR71.3 cr (+49.8%), 9M INR204.3 cr (+59.7%). Order book INR2,967 cr. Q3 order wins only ~INR140 cr (spillover to Q4). Bid pipeline ~INR800 cr. PEC ~INR20 cr (new). Andhra PEC well incident — 2-3 month revenue deferral, rig partially destroyed (insured). QIP paused. Guidance: FY27 revenue growth 30-35%, margin 46-48%, PEC ~INR150 cr/yr by FY27-28. China rig #2 deploys ~early March (Q4). New GAIL contract won. No new Kandla provisioning this FY.

themes.title: Oil & Gas - gas economy (CGD/LNG) + refining/upstream
themes.need: India's gas-economy push now collides with an outright policy reversal. ATGL grew volume 13% to 303 MMSCM and revenue 27% to INR 1,908cr, yet EBITDA FELL sequentially to INR 281cr (~14.7% margin, from INR 310cr) because the government withdrew the pooled-gas mechanism after the West Asia 'peace deal', pushing ATGL to ~15% spot volumes with Brent above $107/bbl; management also noted NWG price is 12% of the Indian crude basket, so a 62% domestic mix protects far less than it looks, and CNG station adds slowed to +5 from +25 in Q4 even as CNG demand grows ~30%. The same shock ran the other way for integrated refining: RELIANCE delivered O2C EBITDA of INR 17,000cr (+17%) THROUGH the Strait-of-Hormuz closure at 96-97% throughput while Asian peers ran 15-20% below capacity, with ethane+ROGC at ~70% of ethylene feed as distillate cracks blew out (gas oil $16 to $63, ATF $14 to $62). MGL/GUJGASLTD/IGL/IRMENERGY carry the same CGD margin squeeze; PETRONET/OIL/ONGC/IOC ride LNG-infra + domestic-gas; CHENNPETRO/MRPL ride GRM cracks; DEEPINDS/JINDRILL/SEAMECLTD on ONGC E&P capex; AEGISLOG/AEGISVOPAK add LPG/gas terminalling.
themes.driver: Whether the pooled/APM gas-allocation mechanism is restored (the single biggest CGD earnings variable); LNG spot price and Brent; GRM/distillate cracks; ONGC rig tenders & day-rates.

hero.oneLiner: Deep Industries is a one-stop oil-and-gas support-services provider of over 30 years' standing that describes itself as India's only integrated onshore and offshore oil & gas service provider, covering more than 70% of post-exploration value-chain services largely on a charter-hire basis.
